title: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks
key_facts: G7 finance ministers and central bank governors agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, said Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama
Agreed at a G7 meeting on the sidelines of the IMF annual gathering in Bangkok, reported 16 Oct 2026 (Thursday remarks)
Follows an IMF warning this week that confidence could be undermined by an AI-enabled attack on a critical service of a financial institution
Simulations will test how authorities respond; results will be used to revise manuals
Exercises could include private financial institutions
Bank of England is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options
quote_evidence: Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said
The results will test effectiveness of existing protocols and be used to revise manuals to better tackle such incidents, the official told reporters.
why_it_matters_hint: The world's biggest economies are rehearsing a response to AI-driven attacks on the financial system.
